faq.title: Renting in Japan: Costs and Application FAQ
faq.subtitle: A guide to renting in Japan
faq.description: Learn about renting in Japan, including application documents, guarantor companies, key money and move-in costs. Property requirements and fees vary.
faq.contactText: Contact us if you have questions about fees or want help finding an option for your budget.

items.question: What is a rent guarantee company?
items.japanese: 保証会社（ほしょうがいしゃ）
items.answer: A company that guarantees rental payment obligations under a separate agreement. If a tenant does not pay, it may pay the landlord within the guarantee's scope and then seek reimbursement. An initial fee and renewal fees may apply. This is not free rent assistance.

items.question: What is rental property insurance?
items.japanese: 火災保険（かさいほけん）
items.answer: Insurance commonly required when signing a rental agreement in Japan. Depending on the plan, it may cover fire, water leaks or liability. Check the coverage, term and fee in the specific policy.

items.question: What is key money?
items.answer: A payment to the landlord required by some rental terms. It is generally non-refundable and applies only when specified for the property.

items.question: What is a security deposit?
items.answer: A deposit paid under the rental agreement. It may be returned after move-out, less valid deductions such as unpaid rent or repairs for which the tenant is responsible.

items.question: What does a property management company do?
items.japanese: 管理会社（かんりがいしゃ）
items.answer: The landlord may appoint a company to handle building matters, receive incident reports and coordinate maintenance. It is not necessarily the owner; its duties depend on the management agreement.

items.question: What is a brokerage fee?
items.japanese: 仲介手数料（ちゅうかいてすうりょう）
items.answer: A fee paid to the real estate company that introduces a property and assists with the rental transaction. The amount depends on the agreement, transaction and applicable rules; it is not the same for every rental.

groups.title: People involved in a rental
groups.subtitle: Know who does what during the rental process.

items.question: Who may be involved when renting a home?
items.answer: There are commonly five roles: the landlord (貸主・大家), property manager (管理会社), brokerage (仲介会社), rent guarantee company (保証会社) and insurer (保険会社). One business may perform more than one role depending on the property and agreements.

items.question: What can upfront costs include?
items.japanese: 初期費用（しょきひよう）
items.answer: They may include advance rent, management fees, security deposit (敷金), key money (礼金), brokerage and guarantee fees, insurance, lock replacement, cleaning and other property-specific charges. Not every home has all of these.

items.question: Are upfront costs always four to six months of rent?
items.answer: No. Four to six months is only a rough reference for some cases, not a fixed rule. Discounts and required fees can change the total. Ask for an itemized estimate before signing.

items.question: How are a security deposit and key money different?
items.answer: A security deposit may be returned after valid deductions under the agreement. Key money is generally non-refundable and is charged only when the property requires it.

items.question: Is the guarantee fee a security deposit?
items.answer: No. A security deposit is paid under the lease; a guarantee fee pays for a service that guarantees payment obligations. Guarantee fees are generally not refunded just because rent was paid on time. Check any recurring fees in the agreement.

items.question: Is the management fee included in rent?
items.answer: It depends on the property. Some include it in the advertised rent, while others charge it separately. Compare the monthly total, including rent, management and recurring fees.

groups.title: Documents and rental agreements
groups.subtitle: Questions about paperwork and the rental process.

items.question: What documents might foreign residents need?
items.answer: Depending on the case: residence card (在留カード), passport (パスポート), proof of income or employment, student ID or proof of enrolment, contact details and other requested documents. Requirements vary by residence status and property.

items.question: Does applying mean I have secured the home?
items.answer: No. An application usually starts screening. Confirm the screening result, agreement terms and contract start date before considering the home secured.

items.question: Can I move in immediately after signing?
items.answer: Not always. The move-in date depends on screening, completion of the contract, payment of required costs and the property's handover schedule.

items.question: Will I get my deposit back when I move out?
items.answer: Some or all may be returned after valid charges under the agreement are reconciled. Unpaid rent, tenant-responsible damage or other valid deductions can reduce the refund.
